# isSlide

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a slide.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isSlide() — Checks whether a value is a slide. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/slide</code> · Since: 1.5.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isSlide(value: unknown): value is GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Slide;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getObjectId`, `getPageElementById`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a slide; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Slide` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const slide = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation().getSlides()[0];

isSlide(slide); // => true
isSlide({}); // => false
isSlide(null); // => false
```
